original_question: Does every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees admit a big Ramsey structure, and is there an exact analogue of the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence that links big Ramsey structures with the topological dynamics of automorphism groups?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.3, read together with Section 2, Question 2.3 and Definition 2.4.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It captures both clauses of the exact open problem: whether finite big Ramsey degrees imply the existence of a big Ramsey structure, and whether there is a KPT-style exact correspondence between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics. This is essentially Problem 6.3 stated almost verbatim.
missing_details: The paper's ambient setting is a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure K; here 'homogeneous' means that every isomorphism between finite substructures extends to an automorphism, and Age(K) denotes the class of its finite substructures.
The hypothesis 'K has finite big Ramsey degrees' means precisely that for every finite substructure A in Age(K), the big Ramsey degree T(A) exists.

A 'big Ramsey structure' is not just any expansion: it is essentially a finite expansion K* of K such that each finite substructure of K* has big Ramsey degree 1, and the unavoidable colorings/canonical partitions cohere when one restricts copies of B to copies of A for A embedding into B.

The dynamics clause is specifically about the topological dynamics of Aut(K), not automorphism groups in general, and the paper asks for an exact correspondence 'in the vein of the KPT-correspondence,' not merely some loose connection.

The nearby context explains that big Ramsey structures imply canonical partitions, while the converse is not known in general; so the question should not be rewritten as if that equivalence were already established.
No ambient ring/field, operator, degree-of-polynomial, or nilpotency hypotheses are involved in this problem; the missing assumptions are structural/Fraisse-theoretic rather than algebraic.
refined_question: Let K be a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure. Assume that K has finite big Ramsey degrees, meaning that for every finite A in Age(K), the big Ramsey degree T(A) exists. Must K carry a big Ramsey structure, namely a finite expansion K* of K such that every finite substructure of K* has big Ramsey degree 1 and the associated unavoidable colorings (canonical partitions) cohere under embeddings A into B in Age(K)? Moreover, is there an exact correspondence, analogous to the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence, between the existence of such big Ramsey structures for K and the topological dynamics of Aut(K)?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 6 rather than any earlier theorem: Problem 6.3 asks, almost word for word, whether every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees carries a big Ramsey structure and whether there is an exact KPT-type dynamical correspondence. To make that question stand alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the Section 2 conventions and definitions: homogeneous means countably infinite homogeneous relational structure; finite big Ramsey degrees means T(A) exists for every finite A in Age(K); and a big Ramsey structure is described via a finite expansion with degree-1 finite substructures and coherent unavoidable colorings/canonical partitions. The paper also stresses that big Ramsey structures imply canonical partitions, but not conversely in general, so no stronger equivalence should be inserted. Theorems 5.4 and 5.5 provide important positive instances, confirming that the intended target is the global open problem, not a broader neighboring question.
